metadata.title: feat(testing): add end-to-end wrapper test workflow for mcpgateway
metadata.author: dima-zakharov

description:
Added workflow to test wrapper with running mcpgateway with fast time server tool.

<!--
For specialized templates, append to your PR URL:
  ?template=feature.md   - New features
Example: https://github.com/IBM/mcp-context-forge/compare/main...your-branch?expand=1&template=bug_fix.md
-->

## 🔗 Related Issue
https://github.com/IBM/mcp-context-forge/issues/1618
Closes #1618 

---

## 📝 Summary

*    Chores
        Added a CI/CD workflow to automate multi-language environment setup, build, service orchestration, and test execution with robust readiness checks and retries.
        Uploads artifacts on failure and supports optional debugging modes to keep services running.

 *   Tests
        Added scripts to run wrapper integration tests (including service health checks and authenticated calls) locally or in CI.

* Adds comprehensive GitHub Actions CI/CD workflow for Rust wrapper testing
* Implement automated testing with gateway, fast-time server, and wrapper integration
* It is possible to run workflow locally with act tool
* JWT token generation with random salt, not dependent on any hard coded values
---

---

## 📓 Notes (optional)
The act may be used for local workflow execution, if the act tool usage is plausible.
```
act --pull=false -W .github/workflows/wrapper.yml
```
The --pull=false means that no docker images should be pulled by act, and this means that no docker hub login is required, but on other hand the images for local workflow execution should be pulled beforehand.
```
docker pull catthehacker/ubuntu:act-latest
```
Currently this feature is not part of the PR, but the comands are simple and they are in this comment.
The workflow starts mcpgateway, compiles fast time server, starts fast time server, creates tools and virutal servers with curl, compiles wrapper and runs the integration test with validation of results.

comments.author: gandhipratik203
comments.body:
Would it be beneficial if we add paths filters to this workflow so it only runs when tools_rust/wrapper/** or .github/workflows/wrapper.yml changes? 

Right now it will run for every PR to main, but this job is fairly heavy since it boots the gateway, builds the Go test server, and builds the Rust wrapper. Scoping it would keep CI cost and noise down without reducing coverage.

reviews.author: crivetimihai
reviews.body: LGTM after rebase and hardening fixes. The E2E workflow design is sound — spawning the wrapper as a child process via rmcp and validating tool discovery + execution through the full stack is a solid integration test approach.

commits.message:
fix(ci): harden wrapper E2E workflow security and consistency

- Add permissions (contents: read), concurrency control, timeout,
  path filtering, and draft-PR skip to match existing workflow patterns
- Mask JWT token in CI logs (::add-mask::) and remove env var dump
  from integration test that leaked the bearer token to stdout
- Add gateway startup failure check (was silently continuing)
- Add tool sync validation (fail if no tools synced)
- Make rmcp an optional dependency behind integration-test feature
  flag so it doesn't bloat the main wrapper binary
- Replace unwrap() with expect() for clear error messages
- Fix is_error.unwrap() -> unwrap_or(false) to prevent panic on None
- Align action versions with existing workflows (v4/v5)
- Use rustup (pre-installed on runners) instead of curl rustup.rs
- Add Cargo target directory caching for faster CI builds
- Remove debug leftovers (set -x, pwd, stat, sleep-3600 step)
- Reduce retry count from 42 to 10 with documented rationale

Signed-off-by: Mihai Criveti <crivetimihai@gmail.com>
